description: Working conditions 是一個很廣的概念，可以涵蓋工時、薪酬、假期、安全、設備、工作量、管理文化、彈性和工作保障。 因此替換前要先判斷是在談 employment terms, physical workplace, social environment, personal job circumstances, or occupational research。

words.example: The union is negotiating for better employment conditions.
words.exampleZh: 工會正爭取更好的僱傭條件。

exercises.original: The union wants to improve working conditions for part-time staff.

exercises.upgrade: The union wants to improve employment conditions for part-time staff.

options.explanation: Employment conditions ✓ — the conditions under which someone is employed, including pay, hours, leave, and security. Here, pay, hours and employment arrangements are central. That makes Employment conditions the most precise replacement for this particular sense of working conditions.

Job conditions — the practical conditions associated with a particular job. This is job-specific and less suitable when the context concerns broad employment systems or formal policy. The decisive clue is that pay, hours and employment arrangements are central.

Employment terms — the specific contractual terms attached to employment. This is contract-focused and too narrow when the context includes physical or social workplace factors. The decisive clue is that pay, hours and employment arrangements are central.
Salary — pay received for work. Salary is only one component of working conditions. The decisive clue is that pay, hours and employment arrangements are central.
Benefits — non-wage employment advantages or entitlements. Benefits are only one component of working conditions. The decisive clue is that pay, hours and employment arrangements are central.
Workload — the amount of work assigned. Workload is only one factor and cannot represent the whole concept. The decisive clue is that pay, hours and employment arrangements are central.

Salary — pay received for work. Salary is only one component of working conditions. The decisive clue is that contract negotiation is explicit.
Benefits — non-wage employment advantages or entitlements. Benefits are only one component of working conditions. The decisive clue is that contract negotiation is explicit.

Employment terms ✓ — the specific contractual terms attached to employment. Here, contract negotiation is explicit. That makes Employment terms the most precise replacement for this particular sense of working conditions.
Working hours — the amount or schedule of time worked. Hours are only one component of working conditions. The decisive clue is that contract negotiation is explicit.

exercises.upgrade: Researchers studied occupational conditions among nurses, drivers and construction workers.

options.explanation: Occupational conditions ✓ — conditions associated with an occupation, especially in research or occupational health. Here, cross-occupation research is central. That makes Occupational conditions the most precise replacement for this particular sense of working conditions.

Conditions of work — a formal labour-policy term for the conditions in which work is carried out. This is formal labour-policy language and can sound too institutional for individual job situations. The decisive clue is that cross-occupation research is central.

Employment conditions — the conditions under which someone is employed, including pay, hours, leave, and security. This is broad and formal, but it can miss a more specific physical, social, contractual, or occupational nuance. The decisive clue is that cross-occupation research is central.
Salary — pay received for work. Salary is only one component of working conditions. The decisive clue is that cross-occupation research is central.
Benefits — non-wage employment advantages or entitlements. Benefits are only one component of working conditions. The decisive clue is that cross-occupation research is central.
Job satisfaction — how satisfied someone feels with their job. This is an attitude or outcome, not the conditions themselves. The decisive clue is that cross-occupation research is central.

exercises.original: The paper links working conditions to long-term health outcomes.
exercises.zh: 論文把職業條件與長期健康結果聯繫起來。
exercises.upgrade: The paper links occupational conditions to long-term health outcomes.
